bug_semantics: The unauthenticated REST endpoint POST /api/v1/livechat/visitor accepts a visitor `name` field and stores it raw (no HTML sanitization server-side). The Omnichannel Queue side panel component apps/meteor/client/views/navigation/sidepanel/omnichannel/InquireSidePanelItem.tsx builds the item subtitle as `${room.lastMessage.u.name || room.lastMessage.u.username}: ${normalizeMessagePreview(room.lastMessage, t)}` — the message body is HTML-escaped inside the normalize helper, but the visitor name is interpolated unescaped — and then renders the whole string through `subtitle={message ? : null}`. An attacker who creates a Livechat visitor with a name containing HTML (e.g. `…`) gets that markup injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML into the DOM of any agent viewing the queue: a real, clickable attacker-controlled link with arbitrary social-engineering text (stored XSS, CWE-79).
flaw_origin: Commit c7db598e9f3c2ad47f6a6be2a9ba7078533c245b ("feat: Enhanced navigation filters (#36049)", 2025-08-15, author Douglas Fabris <devfabris@gmail.com>, committer GitHub squash of PR #36049; parent ebce218aaeca383864cba0e3cd1b9d444196454d) created the file InquireSidePanelItem.tsx in one commit with the entire vulnerable surface: line 31-32 `const message = room.lastMessage && \`${room.lastMessage.u.name || room.lastMessage.u.username}: ${normalizeNavigationMessage(room.lastMessage, t)}\`` (name unescaped; only the message body passes through escapeHTML inside normalizeNavigationMessage) and line 70 `subtitle={message ? <span className='message-body--unstyled' dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: message }} /> : null}` — the advisory's named sink (dangerouslySetInnerHTML rendering of the raw visitor name in the Omnichannel Queue side panel) is born here. The file did not exist at the parent (git show <parent>:<path> fails: 'exists on disk, but not in'). A near-identical copy of the file exists in commit 68f1696e47bffe16a0fb34099e6dc8d41852e119 (2025-08-08, "fix: sanitize `SubscriptionWithRoom` and `ILivechatInquireRecord`") on backup branch origin/feat/sidebar-filters-backup, but that branch was never merged (not an ancestor of 7.10.1 or HEAD), so the first write of the sink in released/affected history is c7db598e; the two versions are byte-identical for this file (git diff empty).

Code archaeology: InquireSidePanelItem.tsx was created by c7db598e (2025-08-15, PR #36049 'Enhanced navigation filters') with both vulnerable components in one commit — the unescaped `${room.lastMessage.u.name || room.lastMessage.u.username}` interpolation and the dangerouslySetInnerHTML subtitle render. Only the message body was escaped (via normalizeNavigationMessage), leaving the attacker-controlled name raw — the exact asymmetry the advisory exploits. BIC = c7db598e: first write of the named sink in released history (file absent at parent ebce218a, verified), single-commit flaw (squash_decomposed=false). A byte-identical earlier copy exists on unmerged backup branch origin/feat/sidebar-filters-backup (68f1696e, 2025-08-08) but never entered any release, so it is not the introducer of the vulnerable released surface. Tag cross-check: the BIC is an ancestor of every affected tag (7.10.1 through 8.7.1), and the fix (mainline b2c16d58, 2026-08-18) is contained in 8.8.0-rc.0/HEAD with per-branch dionisio-bot backports landing in 8.1.8–8.7.1 and 7.10.15 — consistent with the advisory's fixed-version boundaries. AI decision, BIC-only: the BIC commit object carries author Douglas Fabris, committer GitHub (squash), and one Co-authored-by trailer for a human engineer; the marker grep found no AI identity (sentinel NONE-C7DB59). AI-authored commits elsewhere in the repo's history are evidence-only and cannot attribute the BIC. Verdict NOT_AI: a real vulnerability whose flawed design was first written in a human-authored commit. The fix commits themselves are human/bot-authored (Julio Araujo; dionisio-bot backports) and immaterial to attribution regardless.
